messages.subject: All SNPs on multiple chromosomes form singleton linkage groups
parts:
Hello group,

I am working with an F2 plant population (N=180) genotyped at 874 GBS SNPs. This species has 11 chromosomes (plus one unanchored scaffold=CS0). When I try to form linkage groups, all of the SNPs from chromosomes 0, 1, 3, 4, 8 and the last third of 9 form singletons (if I set the minimum LOD score any lower, half of the SNPs form one large linkage group).
> lg<-formLinkageGroups(premap, min.lod=14, max.rf=0.35)

I have attached the LOD/RF plot of the SNPs with their physical map positions.
Why might this happen? Are all the SNPs on these chromosomes the result of sequencing error? If so, what might cause some chromosomes to have almost no variation?

Any advice would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you!

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] All SNPs on multiple chromosomes form singleton linkage groups
parts:
Hard to tell; I'd recommend looking at the 3x3 tables of two-locus genotypes, to see whether markers are looking to be linked or not. You can use the function geno.crosstab().

Here's an example using the fake.f2 data, considering a pair of linked markers and a pair of unlinked ones.

> data(fake.f2)
> mnam1 <- markernames(fake.f2, chr=1)
> mnam2 <- markernames(fake.f2, chr=2)
> geno.crosstab(fake.f2, mnam1[1], mnam1[2])
D1M318
D1M430 - AA AB BB
- 5 9 12 8
AA 3 32 10 0
AB 16 2 63 5
BB 6 1 2 26
> geno.crosstab(fake.f2, mnam1[1], mnam2[1])
D2M359
D1M430 - AA AB BB
- 3 7 16 8
AA 4 15 18 8
AB 16 17 35 18
BB 5 7 15 8

karl
